**Summary of visual evidence:**
- Test image: exposed corn ear with white/gray membranous gall at the top, black spore masses throughout, and orange-yellow kernels visible between the smut galls
- Common_Smut_218 (reference): nearly identical - white/gray smut galls at the ear tip, dark black spore material, exposed yellow kernels
- Other candidates ruled out: Gibberella (pink/red mold), Diplodia (white mold from base), Aspergillus (olive-green powder), Trichoderma (green mold), Head_Smut (black thread masses on tassel)

The white membranous gall with dark black interior at the top of the ear, combined with scattered black teliospore masses among intact kernels, is the defining signature of Common_Smut (*Ustilago maydis*).
